summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with HIV, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a history of MRSA bacteremia and atrial fibrillation was admitted for palpitations and severe Clostridium difficile colitis. She presented with frequent diarrhea and was found to be in atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, likely triggered by dehydration. She received IV fluids, which restored normal sinus rhythm. Oral vancomycin was initiated for C. diff, with improvement in bowel movements during the stay. She completed a hemodialysis session on discharge day and remained on IV vancomycin for ongoing MRSA treatment. Her subtherapeutic INR of 1.2 was noted, with plans to adjust warfarin and recheck INR in three days. She was discharged to extended care to complete antibiotic therapy and ensure close monitoring.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
